elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits inspection to “not more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days’ prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice.”

elements.element: Audits may be conducted only during Customer’s business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is limited to the Company’s normal business hours.

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI’s General Manager, not to an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no confidentiality obligation on HDI’s General Manager or any other auditor.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection are borne by HDI.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause provides no right to shift audit fees to the Company at all, which is more protective of Customer than allowing cost shifting above a 5% threshold.

elements.element: The auditor must have no direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly prohibit direct system access, and the general right to inspect records does not establish that such access is excluded.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause limits inspection to not more than once in any twelve-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days’ prior notice.
elements.evidence: The required 30 days’ prior written notice exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear the fees it incurs in connection with the inspection.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cost-shifting right against the Company, which is more protective than permitting cost shifting above a 10% threshold.

result.reason: The redline adds only the annual frequency cap needed to complete the fallback; the existing 30-day written-notice and HDI-cost provisions already meet or exceed the fallback. It does not reach the preferred position because the operative clause uses HDI’s General Manager rather than an independent auditor, includes no confidentiality obligation, and does not expressly prohibit direct access to Customer systems. The amendment is narrow and does not disturb the inspection scope or related commercial terms.
